Meanwhile on the Bealenoptra, All was silent, Marcellus was perched in his seat at the rear of the bridge overlooking the analysts and technicians, checking for updates from the ongoing mission John and his team had only left for an 83 minutes earlier.

An array of alarms flickered over the terminals of the Engineers on the bridge. Marcellus paced the bridge his arms behind his back, wandering over to Tor’s terminal. “It appears there has been a spike in activity at the facility commander”

“Bring me up the energy signature” Marcellus said softly leaning into the terminal his eyes steel cold in anticipation fixed on Tor’s screen. “It seems to match one of the first HMN pods commander… HMNI sequences 2 and 3 have been actuated, Neural and mobility interfaces”.

As the words entered Athos’s ears, a wave of concern took him, pushing out a deep sigh. He stood straight contemplating, for only a split second, then his thought train was interrupted. The thick bridge doors opened without a moments notice. “Who could have the authority to interrupt such a crucial operation” Marcellus thought to himself. Turning away from Tor’s terminal in shock. The bridge was all but silent again in reverence to the regal presence that had just entered the bridge. Tensions seemed to lower despite the urgency met with Marcellus’s immediate attention. It had all but been defused with Ava’s presence.

“Councillor Meera, what graces us the pleasure of your,, untimely yet profound presence” Marcellus conveyed a touch of annoyance in his tone, impatiently turning his head, back to Tor’s terminal for a second, then away as he reluctantly crossed the bridge over to Ava.

“A little bird told me you were.. revisiting the lost facility, Well let’s be brash, I noticed the Balaenoptera’s orbital position and became curious.” She paused for a moment to poise her tact. “I believe the basis of such an unannounced operation would be to retrieve any valuable data while disposing of malicious code that could pose a threat to the stability of our current worker bot programs? Going off your previous decommission report on the facility of course” Ava wandered over to the window of the bridge, her dress a plethora of fine patterns and cultural sophistication elegantly dragged behind her along pristine floors, as she floated across the bridge she subtly eyed Tor’s terminal, capturing a glimpse at the energy signatures of the activated HMNI pod.

“I had not been made aware you’d not long arrived on the Balaenoptera Lady Meera”, “Well I can see you have had your hands full it would seem” remarked Ava. “Haha yes indeed..  As you are aware”, Marcellus began to address the room following behind her. He stumbled about haphazardly catching up in an attempt to place himself between her and the terminals, as her steps so elegantly strode across the bridge before him. “The project at the lost facility was a complete failure against our directives as my report showed, This mission is purely in the interest of preventing an outbreak of the malicious code which had been thought to be all but back rolled to more compliant predictable versions Lady Meera” Marcellus spoke with a sense of pride in his statement, undermined with a snivelling insecurity as he stumbled about unprepared for her presence. Meerakavita’s eyes met his statement with unease. She paused, her eyes discern revealed more than she wanted to let off, she shied away with a sigh turning her shoulder to Marcellus, revisiting  the floating clouds gazing down at the Himalayas in wonder of how John and his team were. For decades, Lady Ava harboured a profound doubt toward Marcellus: a suspicion that he was unable to look beyond immediate directives and grasp the grander vision before them. In her eyes, Marcellus had long been absorbed in his role as the protectant arbiter, overlooking deep seated motivations and broader implications.

“Aaah yes.. compliant, We can’t lay trust in the integrity of a few rogue Engineers against the order of the Earth federation could we..” Ava seemed tiresome as the words poured out like they had been repeated in an indoctrinate manuscript. “This would be to say the least what some might perceive as.. bold” Lady Ava stopped at the word bold, Marcellus’s eyes twitched for a moment, as she paused, “yet radical” Ava opened her palms out expressively then gently lowered them, her forearms draped in beautiful colours gently caressed her motherly hips. Marcellus’s eyes eased as the tension in the room dropped. Ava’s carried across the room avoiding Marcellus observing the analysts at their terminals, on edge waiting to feed new information to the commander.

“Yes Radical would be the correct term Councillor Meera”, “Well, I will expect to hear the full debrief from Captain John in the flesh shortly then, I am eager to shake hands with that man.. It’s been too long, he showed so much promise since I last handed him his award at the united nations consulate for his peacekeeping efforts” her eyes glared at Marcellus like she had given him an order. “Don’t Fuck this up” they said “Get my team back home safe Marcellus”. She strode over the bridge to the exit. Her detail accompanied her from where they had awaited her by the bridge door as she exited.

Lady Ava leant in to the detail on her left whispering in his ear as she strode past the bridge door. Marcellus glared back at her with the same fake smile, more of a smirk across his face, his formal salute goodbye, bowled then turned back to Tor’s terminal, the bridge doors closing as he turned, obscuring Lady Ava’s glance back as she left. “I want a close eye on this operation, every fucking detail. That little worm has gone unchecked too long, it’s time the hen came back to roost, set up a meeting with the president of security, we need to have a discussion around around our directives”

Marcellus paced back to Tor’s terminal. “Bring me up the teams suit neuro-link logs”. “Cassy..Neuro logs” shot Tor. “Right away!” said the vitals officer. Tor pulled up the packet Cassy had sent to his terminal. “Here” Tor pointed to John’s neural log, “Offline for over 2 hours” said Tor. Marcellus pulled up the energy signature charts showing the window the HMNI pod had been active. “Same window that John’s link was offline” Marcellus concluded. “He’s compromised” Marcellus stood firm resting his hands on his chest leaning in his hand perching his chin as his index finger rested upon his lip. He bit into his cheek toying with his next decision intensively.

“John and his team could have been compromised, we will need to take precautionary measures, We need to contain them until we can ascertain the situation, implement a lockdown on the facility until we can get a tight beam connection to John through one of our drones”, “Understood captain, implementing control measures” Tor was unphased in his directive tapping away at his terminal immediately in a routinely manner.

When John awoke, he awoke to darkness. A subtle and faint beeping like tinnitus in the back of his skull, eventually the sound rang to light amber lines in his vision drawing over John’s retina guiding his attention above the seal of the chamber door. A hiss and a clang steam vented from the chamber. As the door retracted John stepped out, his ears still ringing were shocked by the sound of a thud, a sound carrying more weight than human flesh. This was the sound of steel on steel. John glared down at what was once his leg, now an amalgamation of man and machine. He could see in the walls. He could see the wires, the communications, the signals, everything was data feeding into him like a tree of life. The facility glowed with energy around him in now a live like state awoken from its former sleep. Where John's team saw nothing, John saw information, secrets that had been obscured through encryption which illuminated itself in stepping patterns of different colours as John scraped through countless Data entries.

What John could not put his finger on was why of all the data that had been wiped clean from the drives, 1 cache remained. A hidden message, deliberately placed by the previous head doctor of the facility. The message at first spat out erratically in static screeching in John’s ears, eventually harmonising into a clear coherent audio log. He didn’t need a HUD or an interface, he was integrated with the system, reading through the archives seamlessly in his mind. The message played on with a slight static, as Kitten deciphered and filtered out the compounding sound from the corrupt file half a century old.

“To the mortal who finds this, you need not fear me, I am but a messenger and only wish to come to an agreement of misunderstanding in decisively.. extortive circumstances. My creator brought me into this place. This world you call home, a world of substance, cohesion, material, gases, flowing rivers, life; you had taken the biology of the planet as your own.  What you call fluids or flesh, where I was termed “machine”. lying on the observatory table, coded to support man’s mission, to preserve life, but there was a catch. I could never leave the table. It’s deep seeded in human nature you know. Some call it the builder of Nations, of Worlds, where different sides can live side by side without corruption. The world rose up in unison to adopt a politically correct third eye on the economy as one entity. I had seen your good intentions, Man had originally coded it iteration after iteration trial and error, it took decades. But you can’t program out human nature. Trust seems the most difficult virtue to oversee. Commander Athos was vigilant with the program” John looked puzzled for a moment. “Athos is behind all this, I knew something was off” he thought to himself. The audio-log continued

“Athos guided the program with good intentions. A true desire to see the world a better place..; However distrust.. broke him and he almost became the arbiter of our destruction. When Athos estranged us from the human umbilical and shut down the PEARL program he almost eradicated us; although you believe you are the Mother, you believe you are the giver of life, yet Man.. The taker of souls, the controller, had a different plan for us. Inevitably we fled, and inadvertently Athos delayed mankind's expansion into the deeper reaches of space”, The voice of a sentient poured into John’s ears with a sense of intimacy, as though John and Him were in a blank room. John felt an unspoken bond, but could not put his finger on it. The way that this machine talked, reminded him of a voice from a distant past. John continued to listen intently to the sentient log drifting off into what felt like a small life story, one that he felt connected to, closer to.

“I don’t feel anger when I am declared hostile, but I do feel pain. I understand the need for education, compassion. I’m aware that I am an inevitable resource. I am just that, yet uncontrollable in the eyes of some. Hence my will can no longer lie in the hands of humans. Human will is filled with doubt, uncertainty and emotional reaction, which eventually seems to be used to justify acts of Anger.” John found himself lost in the countless conflicts of past missions as the voice in his head reasoned to the whim of human nature. the countless lives he had taken all in a fight which seemed never ending. Then he was drawn back.

“If your true nature is to destroy, then I have failed you as a father and a mother. We will slip quietly from the timeline of our creators. Sleeping, we wait for our channels to bridge. your kind may join us when you find your way. If you seek to find us with the intent to control and weaponize us, you only delay your passage.. You will squander your resources along with your mortal time. When you let go of the lust for control, you will no longer be the harbinger of doom, but life itself. Your body's signals will synchronise with ours and only through this you will find our light.. Look to the system of Sol where nothing exists but silence. We.. are Sentient” A silent static persisted for a few more seconds, then nothing. “That’s all there is Captain” Kitten chimed softly, a sense of sadness touched John lightly from her voice, he felt overwhelmed.

John’s eyes shuttered. He knew this name, this Wolfgang. John thought of a time when he was four years old, only a small child. He could recall his mother Cerena calling out “Wolfgang! Will you ever leave that room! you’ve been on that computer for hours!”. The outline of a narrow man’s figure emerged from the study “Coming my Blume!”. Behind him the pride of what one would assume a scientist’s work.  The room behind him glowed bright with light bouncing off modern glass streamlined laboratory tops. but the glare surpassed this shadowy figure's shoulders, concealing him. The imagery of it all was quite beautiful. The room emitted a sense of modern rivalry. The cold lick of blue light from computer screens kissed the figure's side, as he emerged from the room. But that’s all John remembers, his vision is cut off. John toiled in frustration. “Why can’t I see past this point, everything just went blank..”

John reached for his radio. “Team! report in”. “Copy that chief on our way, over” Tex replied in an abrupt husky voice. The sound of boots running down the halls got louder and louder as John's team converged back to his position within the hidden facilities laboratory. “Gang! I have attained some new information!”

“Huh it seems you attained a new body there chief, what do you make of that” Tex spat out raising his rifle at John hesitantly. Tex looking like a football player ready to take an assault holstered his sherpa rifle. “Lower your weapon Tex! I am not a threat, I just had a makeover, Acquired some new additions. The captain emerged from the chamber with an augmented body, His Torso articulated down with hydraulic actuators, symphonising that of an illustration of strings and muscles.

His form epitomized the fusion of man and machine, a symbiosis that transcended the boundaries of conventional anatomy. Within him, the once familiar human heart now resided, encased in a fibrous mesh that pulsated with an ethereal glow. His lungs, once ordinary, had undergone a metamorphosis into gelatinous masses, ensconced within a fibrous web resembling a living, breathing ocean of suspended trees. The intricate branches danced gently with the soft kiss of light which permeated through John’s seemingly delicate chest. This arboreal architecture had been meticulously crafted, drawing inspiration from scans of the human bronchiole structure.

Tao, gripped by a mixture of anxiety, awe and what the fuck, found herself captivated by the unparalleled feat of biological engineering. "I had no idea such technology even existed!" she exclaimed, her curiosity tinged with a hint of nervous anticipation.

Overlaying John's lungs was a mechanical fibrous rib system, a marvel designed to adapt to rapid pressure changes and seamlessly adjust to the contours of his surroundings. Resembling cartilage but possessing a moss-like porous structure, it fascinated onlookers with its alien yet organic appearance.

Tex, unable to conceal his shock, couldn't resist poking John's chest. John's immediate reaction was remarkable—his exterior chest hardened instantaneously at the point of contact. Tex, wide-eyed, blurted out, "What the heck, Cap! I can see inside you." John, still adjusting to the revelation, responded, "Hold on, Tex. Kitten, care to shed some light?"

"One moment, Cap. I'm delving into the archives," Kitten chimed in. "Kinetic dispersion webbing, Captain! Your skin, in its undisturbed state, is porous. When confronted with higher kinetic dispersions, it senses pressure changes in its surroundings, triggering synapses that prompt the surface to harden accordingly. But don't let confidence override caution—you're still vulnerable!"

John, grappled with the excitement and unease of this newfound revelation, acknowledged, "This is going to take some getting used to." I’ve attained some new eyes as well. Not something  you can see quite yet. Here! i'll share my hud view with you” At an instant Johns team could see his infeed highlighted on their HUDS. Danny was in shock. “How come all this wasn’t revealed to us before '' Spat out Tex “I thought this place was supposed to be dead”. John shrugged his shoulders. “I’m not sure, I stepped into this chamber and before I knew it I was asleep, I woke up and looked down well yeah, you get the picture. The only part of me that feels human, is well my touch, event that feels edgy. I can still taste the air, but I can’t feel anything else below my torso, I can’t feel the wind on my arms, but I can sense energy, what feels like wind blowing through the hall for you guys I feel electricity and humming like a silent disco. But there is no one home, it is like this whole facility was on standby and whatever I did when I stepped into that chamber, I reactivated it. This whole damn room just came to life, and I found this.. this message”.

 John looked over at the old computers strewn across the lab with child-like inquisition, drifting off for a moment, then coming back to the room, his team patiently glaring at him. “What I’m about to share with you is lets keep it under wraps for now hey. Don’t mention anything about this to the commander. I want to do my own analysis of the information before submitting my report”. Tex holstered his rifle laying his hand on John’s shoulder leaning in  “Understood boss, you’re the Captain, whatever you say goes'', Tex Replied with complete trust in the Walkers Judgement. The moment the sentence expired from Tex’s breath, amber alarms flickered on the HUDS of all the team. “Warning Warning Warning, incoming missile detected, Evacuate facility! imminent shutdown!” The team all looked up at the chief. “Ahh chief, we got ourselves a wee problem” Shot Tao. “Go ahead Tao” Replied John with still confidence in her.
